recommendation: Keep the audit commit in core. If the external subscriptions guide does not preserve the FHIR-30429 token policy clarification, follow up in that guide, preferably with the pending FHIR-47290 external-guide work.
issue_request: FHIR-30429 was a Published/Persuasive R5 core Subscription clarification asking whether a websocket binding token can be reused after reconnect; the approved resolution was to document that behavior is server/implementation-dependent, including single-use and reusable-until-expiration policies.
initial_application: Core commit 63ac0d8b02 applied the issue by adding implementation-dependent token-security wording to OperationDefinition/Subscription-get-ws-binding-token and adding Subscription notes about single-use, reusable-until-expiration, single-client/shared token policies, and server documentation of issuance policy.
additional_context: Current R6 core has Subscription active, but the Subscription operations list now excludes $get-ws-binding-token and the channel prose points websocket details to the FHIR Subscriptions Backport IG. R6 history deleted the operation and noted websocket content moving to external sources; FHIR-47290 later records that the operation and websocket details are moving to an external guide. Related backport Jira and Zulip evidence show the operation is part of the subscriptions/backport websocket workflow rather than a current core-owned detail.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No core source was changed because reintroducing token lifecycle guidance in current core would restore details for an operation current core no longer publishes.
